text:
jess: folx, ACME is seeing intermittent truncated SSE responses when their client reconnects. They say final tokens are missing or appear duplicated after a reconnect. Ticket #2345 has a pcap attached. Escalating for triage :frowning:

marco: can you paste the pcap link and a minimal repro? need to reproduce before digging into runtime.

jess: pcap uploaded here: https://internal-pcaps/redwood/2345.pcapng

jess: repro steps from the customer (copied):
1) open SSE connection to /v1/streams with Authorization bearer token
2) stream until model emits final tokens
3) client simulates network glitch, closes TCP, then reconnects with same resume token
4) sometimes server sends a truncated tail or duplicate fragments

ingrid: are they using prefix/KV caching or any custom routing? that can cause odd resume behaviours when caches are evicted.

eli: quick metrics snapshot: at the time of the customer incident we saw a ~2% spike in 5xxs for the SSE pool and connection churn went up ~30%. CPU/GPU utilization steady. network errors elevated for that edge region.

repro-bot: pcap quick summary: saw quick TCP close from client then SYN to reconnect; on server side there's a TLS close_notify then immediate RST within ~120ms in some flows. also saw some duplicate SSE events across two connections.

marco: interesting — duplicate events + RST suggests we might be emitting the same pending buffer while the old connection hasn't fully quiesced. could be a race in the resume/owner swap logic.

marco: can someone try a local repro with a tight reconnect loop? here's a simple curl-based check that sometimes reproduces token loss for me:

```
# keep-alive + manual reconnect
while true; do
  curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=rt-legacy" || sleep 0.1
done
```

jess: @marco i ran that once with the customer's resume-token and reproduced a truncated final event. saved tcpdump + app logs. uploaded to the ticket.

ingrid: two actionable hypotheses: (A) prefix/KV cache eviction causes resume token to be interpreted as pointing to truncated buffer; (B) token refresh/auth race results in auth 401 and server tearing the stream mid-write which triggers partial outputs on reconnect. both are plausible.

eli: i dug into auth logs — there are a handful of 401s for that tenant within the same minute as reconnects. token refresh TTL is short (60s) for their integration. small chance client refresh race causes the server to prematurely invalidate the session.

marco: overlaying traces shows cases with: "resume_token=abc123" followed by next connection with same resume_token but server-side kvcache_hit=false. stack shows eviction path `kvcache.evict()` within 200ms of disconnect. if the client reconnects rapidly we lose backing state.

marco: short-term mitigation: disable prefix caching for that tenant and force server to stream from model state (slower but consistent). config snippet to push to rollout api:

```
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "streaming": {
    "prefix_cache": false
  }
}
```

ingrid: i'll prepare a canary to disable prefix_cache for this tenant and watch SSE 5xx and truncated-event rates. eli please add more tracing fields for the stream path (`stream.conn_id`, `sse.resume_token`, `kvcache_hit`).

eli: on it. also increasing heartbeat interval can help reduce rapid reconnect churn — suggest bumping from 10s to 30s for their tenant temporarily.

jess: another customer note: they saw a sudden billing bump during their reconnect stress test. could duplicate chunk replay be causing double-counting of tokens on reconnect? filing billing follow-up with finance.

marco: duplicate chunk replay could increment token counters if we reprocess some final tokens twice before we detect dedupe. we'll add a dedupe-pass on resume that checks `resume_token` + last_emitted_seq.

repro-bot: attached pcap analysis gist: https://internal-pcaps/redwood/2345-analysis.txt — shows RST timings and sequence gaps.

eli: next steps i have: add the extra logs, deploy canary disabling prefix_cache for acme, and instrument token-count path for reconnects to confirm billing double-counting.

ingrid: i'll coordinate the canary and watch the real-time dashboard for SSE truncated-event rate, 5xx rate, and connection churn.

jess: i'll update the customer with ETA and ask them to hold any heavy reconnect loops for now. thanks team :thumbsup:

marco: if the canary looks good we'll push a short-term fix disabling prefix cache + a follow-up patch to the resume path to make it resilient to eviction races.

jess: noted. saving all logs and pcap links into ticket #2345 and will keep thread updated.

eli: posted a dashboard snapshot link: https://dashboards.redwood/streams/acme/2345

jess: closing the loop here for now. will reopen if canary shows regressions.
